name: Abacavir
indication: HIV infection as part of antiretroviral therapy (ART)
warnings: ⚠ Contraindicated in patients with HLA-B*5701 mutation (risk of hypersensitivity reaction)
⚠ Use as part of combination ART only — do not use as monotherapy

name: Aciclovir
warnings: ⚠ Use age-specific dosing: >1 month to 1 year: 12.5 mg/kg; >1–6 years: 10 mg/kg; >6–12 years: 6 mg/kg

name: Adrenaline
indication: Anaphylaxis, cardiac arrest, croup, septic shock

name: Albendazole
warnings: ⚠ Avoid in children under 6 months unless under specialist supervision

name: Albumin
frequency: Single dose or repeat as per clinical need

name: Alfacalcidol
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in neonates and preterm infants

name: Alprostadil
indication: Maintain ductal patency in duct-dependent lesions
warnings: ⚠ Contraindicated in neonates with severe respiratory distress syndrome

name: Amikacin
warnings: ⚠ Adjust dosing interval for neonates and preterm infants based on gestational age

name: Amlodipine
warnings: ⚠ Approved for use in children ≥6 years; limited data under 6 years

name: Amiodarone
warnings: ⚠ Use with extreme caution in infants and neonates; off-label use under specialist supervision

name: Amitriptyline
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended in children under 12 years

name: Amoxicillin
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in infants <3 months; reduce maximum daily dose due to immature renal clearance

name: Amoxicillin/Clavulanic Acid (Augmentin)
indication: Otitis media, sinusitis, lower respiratory infections, skin and soft tissue infections
warnings: ⚠ Use weight-band-based dosing in infants and young children: e.g., >2.5–3.5 kg (for 1–3 months), >3.5–5 kg (for 3–6 months), etc.
⚠ Dose must be adjusted for neonates and infants <3 months due to immature renal function
⚠ Use with caution in children <2 months unless directed by a specialist

name: Ampicillin
frequency: 8–12 hourly depending on age and gestation
warnings: ⚠ Dosing interval must be adjusted for preterm and low birth weight neonates

name: Amphotericin B
warnings: ⚠ Limited data in neonates; use with caution and monitor closely

name: Artemether/lumefantrine
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended in infants <2 months or <5 kg

name: Aspirin
warnings: ⚠ Avoid in children <12 years due to risk of Reye's syndrome unless specifically indicated (e.g. Kawasaki disease)
⚠ Use lowest effective dose for shortest possible duration

name: Atazanavir/ritonavir (ATV/r)
warnings: ⚠ Avoid in infants <3 months or <5 kg due to risk of kernicterus

name: Atenolol
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in children <6 years; limited data available

name: Atropine
warnings: ⚠ Avoid ophthalmic use in infants <3 months due to risk of systemic toxicity

name: Azathioprine
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in children <1 year; dosing must be individualized and closely monitored

name: Ceftriaxone
warnings: ⚠ Contraindicated in neonates ≤28 days with jaundice, hypoalbuminaemia, or requiring IV calcium
⚠ Avoid in premature neonates ≤41 weeks postmenstrual age

name: Gentamicin
warnings: ⚠ Dosing interval must be adjusted based on gestational and postnatal age

name: Paracetamol
warnings: ⚠ Reduce dose in chronically ill or malnourished children
⚠ Use age-specific maximum daily dose: lower limits in neonates and preterm infants

name: Baclofen
indication: Spasticity in cerebral palsy or spinal cord injury
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in children under 2 years due to limited safety data

name: Beclomethasone
warnings: ⚠ Most formulations approved for children ≥6 years; use under 6 years requires spacer and supervision

name: Benzathine benzylpenicillin
frequency: Single IM dose or every 3–4 weeks
warnings: ⚠ For neonates <3 kg or <30 days: specialist consultation required for safe dosing

name: Benzodiazepines (diazepam)
warnings: ⚠ Not for long-term use in children or adolescents
⚠ Dose must be adjusted based on age: max 5 mg/day if <5 years, 10 mg/day if >5 years

name: Benzylpenicillin (Penicillin G)
warnings: ⚠ Adjust dose and interval in neonates and premature infants according to gestational age

name: Betamethasone
frequency: Apply thinly once or twice daily
warnings: ⚠ Use age-based dosing in palliative care: <1 yr (250 mcg 8 hourly), 1–5 yrs (1 mg 8 hourly), etc.

name: Biperiden
warnings: ⚠ Use age-specific doses: 1–6 years (2 mg), 7–10 years (3 mg), >10 years (5 mg)

name: Boomslang antivenom
warnings: ⚠ Specialist consultation recommended in infants and small children

name: Budesonide
warnings: ⚠ Use with spacer device in children <5 years; monitor growth with prolonged use

name: Bupivacaine
warnings: ⚠ Max dose is 2 mg/kg in infants <12 months, overweight children, or those with liver disease

name: Caffeine citrate
frequency: Loading dose, then maintenance every 24 hours
warnings: ⚠ Indicated only for preterm infants with apnoea of prematurity; not for term infants

name: Calcium gluconate
indication: Symptomatic or acute hypocalcaemia, cardiac membrane stabilisation
frequency: 6–8 hourly or as needed in emergencies

name: Carbamazepine
warnings: ⚠ Avoid in patients with absence or myoclonic seizures
⚠ Avoid in patients on antiretrovirals (e.g., NNRTIs, PIs, InSTIs) due to CYP450 interactions

name: Chlorpheniramine
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in children <2 years due to risk of sedation and respiratory depression

name: Ciprofloxacin
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in children due to risk of arthropathy; restrict to specialist indications

name: Clonazepam
warnings: ⚠ Long-term use requires specialist monitoring due to sedation and dependence risk

name: Cotrimoxazole
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in neonates <6 weeks due to risk of kernicterus from sulfa component

name: Cyanocobalamin (Vitamin B12)
frequency: Once daily or weekly depending on severity

name: Dexamethasone
warnings: ⚠ Avoid in patients with herpes or measles infection unless benefit outweighs risk

name: Dexchlorpheniramine
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in children <2 years due to sedative and anticholinergic effects

name: Diazepam
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended for long-term use in children and adolescents
⚠ Max 5 mg/day for children <5 years; 10 mg/day for >5 years
⚠ Avoid rectal/IV route in infants <6 months unless in emergency

name: Diclofenac
warnings: ⚠ Avoid in children <6 months
⚠ Caution with dehydration or renal impairment

name: Digoxin
warnings: ⚠ Close monitoring required in neonates and infants due to narrow therapeutic window

name: Dimenhydrinate
warnings: ⚠ Use not recommended in children <2 years due to anticholinergic toxicity risk

name: Diphenhydramine
warnings: ⚠ Contraindicated in children <2 years due to respiratory depression risk

name: Doxycycline
warnings: ⚠ Contraindicated in children <8 years unless benefit outweighs risk (e.g., RMSF, leptospirosis)
⚠ Risk of tooth discoloration and enamel hypoplasia

name: Erythromycin
indication: Penicillin allergy alternative, pertussis, neonatal conjunctivitis
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in neonates due to risk of pyloric stenosis, especially with oral erythromycin

name: Ferrous sulphate
warnings: ⚠ Oral iron dosing must be adjusted in children <6 months; use caution to avoid overdose

name: Fluconazole
warnings: ⚠ Neonatal dosing requires longer intervals (every 72 hrs in first week of life)

name: Fludrocortisone
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in neonates; monitor electrolytes and blood pressure closely

name: Flumazenil
frequency: Single IV dose (may repeat after 1 min)
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended for routine use in children due to seizure risk, especially in chronic benzodiazepine users

name: Fluoxetine
warnings: ⚠ Use generally limited to children ≥8 years; monitor for suicidal ideation

name: Fluticasone
warnings: ⚠ Use age-specific dosing: <12 years (1 spray per nostril daily); ≥12 years (2 sprays per nostril daily)
⚠ Monitor growth with prolonged use in children

name: Furosemide
warnings: ⚠ Neonatal and infant doses must be lower; max chronic dose 6 mg/kg/day
⚠ Risk of ototoxicity at high doses or rapid IV administration

name: Gentamicin
warnings: ⚠ Dosing interval and serum level monitoring essential in neonates and preterms due to risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity

name: Griseofulvin
indication: Tinea capitis and other dermatophyte infections
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended for children under 2 years

name: Haloperidol
warnings: ⚠ Use age- and weight-specific dosing: <12 years use 0.01–0.1 mg/kg/day; >12 years max 5 mg/dose
⚠ Avoid in children under 3 years unless specialist supervised

name: Heparin
frequency: IV bolus, infusion, or line flush
warnings: ⚠ Neonatal dosing requires careful monitoring of aPTT; risk of bleeding in low-weight infants

name: Hydralazine
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in neonates and infants due to risk of hypotension

name: Hydroxyurea
warnings: ⚠ Requires specialist supervision; dosing adjusted based on age, weight, and blood count response

name: Hyoscine butylbromide
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended for children under 6 years
⚠ Use age-based dosing for palliative care: <4 years, 5–11 years, ≥12 years

name: Insulin (short-acting)
frequency: Hourly IV infusion (DKA) or per glucose monitoring
warnings: ⚠ Requires specialist supervision in neonates and infants; risk of hypoglycaemia and electrolyte shifts

name: Insulin (long-acting)
warnings: ⚠ Use only under paediatric endocrinologist supervision in young children

name: Isoniazid
warnings: ⚠ Pyridoxine supplementation required in children <5 years, malnourished, or HIV-positive
⚠ Monitor liver function in infants and neonates

name: Ivermectin
frequency: Once, repeat in 7 days if needed
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended for children weighing <15 kg
⚠ Avoid in children under 5 years

name: Ketamine
warnings: ⚠ Avoid in children with obstructive sleep apnoea
⚠ IM route is painful; avoid unless necessary

name: Ketoconazole
warnings: ⚠ Avoid use in children <2 years unless directed by a healthcare provider

name: Lamivudine
warnings: ⚠ Dose and formulation must be adjusted in children <3 months
⚠ Adult dosing applies only ≥30 kg or ≥10 years

name: Levetiracetam
warnings: ⚠ Use age-specific dosing: 1–6 months, ≥6 months to <4 years, ≥4 years
⚠ Start low and titrate gradually in younger children

name: Lopinavir/ritonavir (LPV/r)
warnings: ⚠ Use only in children ≥14 days old and ≥2 kg
⚠ Oral solution contains alcohol and propylene glycol—monitor for toxicity in neonates

name: Lorazepam
warnings: ⚠ Neonatal use requires dose adjustment and cardiorespiratory monitoring

name: Magnesium sulphate
warnings: ⚠ IV use requires close monitoring for respiratory depression and hypotension in infants

name: Metformin
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended for children <10 years
⚠ Use only in overweight/obese adolescents with insulin resistance under supervision

name: Metronidazole
warnings: ⚠ Use reduced frequency in neonates due to immature hepatic metabolism

name: Morphine
indication: Moderate to severe pain, palliative care
warnings: ⚠ Use age- and route-specific dosing: neonates, infants, and children have different bolus and infusion needs
⚠ Risk of respiratory depression in neonates and opioid-naive children

name: Mupirocin
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended in infants <2 months unless directed by a healthcare provider

name: Naloxone
warnings: ⚠ Shorter duration of action than most opioids; observe child for at least 12 hours post-administration
⚠ Use with caution in neonates; withdrawal symptoms may be severe

name: Nevirapine
frequency: Once or twice daily depending on regimen
warnings: ⚠ Dose is age- and weight-specific: different for birth to 6 weeks, 6 weeks–6 months, 6–9 months, and >9 months
⚠ Increased risk of severe rash and hepatotoxicity in infants <6 weeks

name: Nifedipine
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in infants; limited data on safety and efficacy under 1 year of age

name: Nitrofurantoin
warnings: ⚠ Contraindicated in infants <1 month due to risk of haemolytic anaemia

name: Nystatin
warnings: ⚠ Use oral suspension carefully in neonates to avoid aspiration

name: Ondansetron
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in infants <6 months; limited safety data
⚠ Monitor QT interval in all age groups with repeated dosing

name: Oral rehydration solution (ORS)
frequency: Per stool loss or maintenance therapy

name: Phenobarbitone
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended as maintenance therapy for children >2 years due to cognitive side effects
⚠ Still used in neonates and infants under 6 months for acute seizure control

name: Phenytoin
frequency: Loading then once or twice daily maintenance
warnings: ⚠ Avoid in neonates and preterm infants unless under specialist supervision
⚠ Risk of hypotension and arrhythmias with IV bolus

name: Piperacillin/tazobactam
warnings: ⚠ Neonatal and infant dosing requires careful adjustment due to immature renal clearance

name: Prednisone
warnings: ⚠ Max dose by age for croup: <2 years (20 mg), 2–5 years (30 mg), 6–12 years (40 mg)
⚠ Prolonged use may cause growth suppression and adrenal suppression

name: Promethazine
warnings: ⚠ Contraindicated in children <2 years due to risk of fatal respiratory depression
⚠ Avoid oral use in children <6 years when possible

name: Propranolol
warnings: ⚠ Contraindicated in children with asthma or bradycardia
⚠ Use with caution in infants and monitor for hypoglycaemia

name: Pyridoxine
warnings: ⚠ Dose is age-based in TB protocols: <5 years (12.5 mg), ≥5 years (25 mg)

name: Rifampicin
warnings: ⚠ Dosing and duration depend on age and weight band
⚠ Requires monitoring of liver function in young children

name: Risperidone
indication: Behavioural disorders, psychosis, autism spectrum disorders
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended for children <5 years
⚠ Use weight-based dosing for children: e.g., <20 kg (start 0.25 mg), >20 kg (start 0.5 mg)
⚠ Monitor for extrapyramidal symptoms and weight gain

name: Salbutamol
warnings: ⚠ Spacer device recommended in children <5 years

name: Sodium bicarbonate
frequency: Single IV dose or infusion depending on pH
warnings: ⚠ Use with caution in neonates and small infants
⚠ Do not administer concurrently with calcium-containing solutions

name: Sodium valproate
warnings: ⚠ Avoid in adolescent girls and preadolescent females unless no alternatives exist
⚠ Monitor liver function in children <2 years

name: Spironolactone
warnings: ⚠ Hyperkalaemia risk is higher in neonates and infants—monitor electrolytes

name: Streptomycin
warnings: ⚠ Avoid in neonates and infants unless benefits outweigh risks due to ototoxicity

name: Sulfasalazine
indication: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease
warnings: ⚠ Contraindicated in children <2 years
⚠ Monitor for blood dyscrasias and liver toxicity during long-term use

name: Tenofovir
warnings: ⚠ Not recommended for children <10 years or <30 kg
⚠ Monitor renal function and bone density in adolescents

name: Tetracycline (topical)
warnings: ⚠ Systemic use of tetracyclines is contraindicated <8 years; topical forms are generally safe

name: Theophylline
warnings: ⚠ Narrow therapeutic index; serum level monitoring essential
⚠ Dose must be titrated individually; avoid in children <1 year unless under specialist care

name: Timolol (topical)
warnings: ⚠ Risk of systemic absorption and bradycardia in neonates and infants—monitor closely

name: Vancomycin
warnings: ⚠ Neonates require longer dosing intervals (e.g., every 12–18 hrs)
⚠ Monitor serum levels closely in neonates and infants due to risk of nephrotoxicity

name: Vitamin A
frequency: Single dose on Day 1 and repeat on Day 2 if needed
warnings: ⚠ Dosing is age- and weight-specific: different doses for <6 months, 6–11 months, and ≥12 months
⚠ Avoid repeat dosing in neonates unless under specialist direction

name: Vitamin D (Cholecalciferol)
warnings: ⚠ Monitor serum calcium and phosphate levels in neonates and infants during therapy

name: Vitamin K (Phytomenadione)
indication: Bleeding due to deficiency or prevention in neonates
warnings: ⚠ Dosage and route are age-specific: neonates typically receive 0.5–1 mg IM at birth

name: Warfarin
warnings: ⚠ Not routinely used in neonates or infants without specialist guidance
⚠ Requires regular INR monitoring and dose adjustment
⚠ Interacts with many drugs and foods — closely monitor

name: Zidovudine (AZT)
warnings: ⚠ Neonatal dosing is based on gestational age and birth weight: different schedules for <35 weeks and <2.5 kg
⚠ Adult dose applies only to ≥10 years and ≥30 kg
